title: d1-run-spec-validation report (also the pack's validation/rule-outcomes.jsonl source)
description: Whether the legacy application actually behaves as the lifted rules say. Rule-level rather than scenario-level on purpose: a scenario pass rate says nothing about whether a behavior's EL lifts were among the scenarios that ran, and those lifts are the framework's headline claim. See docs/phase-d-spec-validation.md.

status.description: fail when any outcome is contradicted. not_exercised does not fail the step — it is a recorded finding about the fixture set or the extraction, and failing on it would push teams toward deleting the case rather than fixing the data.

scope.description: framework.yaml: spec_validation_scope as actually run. Recorded so a report cannot be read as more thorough than the run that produced it.

counts.description: rules_total is every active lifted RULE in the pack, not every rule in scope — the ratio of out_of_scope to rules_total is the number that says how much of the framework's central claim went unchecked, and it is only legible if the denominator is the whole population.

browser.description: What drove the run. Recorded because a visibility assertion is a browser-behaviour claim as much as an application one, and a report without it cannot be reproduced.

outcomes.description: Exactly one entry per active lifted RULE node, including those out of scope. A rule with no entry is an unreported rule, which is the state this whole step exists to make impossible.

source_node_id.description: The node the rule was lifted from, via its DERIVED_FROM edge.

source_kind.description: Echoed from a3-lift-rule, plus `nav` for a rule lifted from a NAV node's condition. This is what makes the report readable: an el-derived rule reported out_of_scope is a claim nothing checked, while a computation-derived one still has c4's branch coverage behind it.

outcome.description: validated: a case exercised the rule and the app agreed. contradicted: it did not — the SPEC is wrong, blocking the owning behavior and routing to a3-lift-rule review. not_exercised: a case exists but the state was unreachable, or the EL attribute has no browser-observable assertion. out_of_scope: excluded by scope, counted, and seeded into the open-questions register by c9.

cases.description: The rendered cases that targeted this rule, by scenario or decision-table-row id. Several for a rule with a decision table — one per reduced row — and the rule is validated only when every one of them is.

detail.description: For a fail: what was asserted and what was observed. This is the text a human reads when deciding whether the lift or the fixture was wrong, so an assertion diff belongs here rather than a stack trace.

reason.description: Required in substance for not_exercised and out_of_scope: which state could not be reached and why, or which scope rule excluded it. Null is acceptable only for validated. A not_exercised with no reason is indistinguishable from a case nobody wrote.

open_question_id.description: Set by c9 when this outcome seeded an unvalidated_lifted_rule entry. Null before assembly.
